deep.reconstruction:
There is no derivation on this page. It is a wrapper or label sheet, not a working page.

(1) Ink heading: 'Crelle. Journal für reine und angewandte Mathematik. Bd. 32. Berlin 1846.' This is a bibliographic reference to volume 32 of Crelle's Journal (1846). The sheet probably wrapped a note or excerpt connected with that volume. It may also have wrapped an offprint or a page reference.

(2) Ink signature lower right: 'L. Riemann' or possibly 'B. Riemann', followed by a parenthetical abbreviation read as '(Mykl.)'. The abbreviation's reading is uncertain. The hand looks like a later archival or ownership annotation rather than a mathematical note.

(3) Red archival or shelf mark lower left: read as 'Ms. S. 58' / 'Nm. 5.58'.

(4) Small pencil folio number '51' at upper right. Two short pencil dashes sit under the end of the heading.

(5) Pencil sketch, not in the machine transcription. A curved arc rises from a point at the lower left. A nearly straight, slightly concave line runs from the same point to the right, so the two meet at a sharp cusp-like angle (a horn angle, i.e. curve and line nearly tangent at the vertex). A separate, nearly vertical line crosses the right end of the horizontal stroke. The result looks like a curvilinear triangle with one zero or very small angle, partly cut by a transversal. There are no labels, formulas or text attached. Any mathematical reading, such as a triangle with a zero angle, a domain for conformal mapping, or a horn angle, would be speculation. Volume 32 of Crelle contains papers by Jacobi, Kummer, Eisenstein and others. Which paper, if any, the sheet refers to cannot be determined from this page alone.
